newsitem.title: UK: Yorks Water asked to stop some abstractions.
newsitem.headline: Yorks Water asked to stop some abstractions.

text.p: The government has asked Yorkshire Water Plc to stop taking extra water from certain rivers in a process known as "abstraction" as the company improves its own water grid.
A statement from the Environment Agency said it had asked the company for surrender five short-term abstraction licences granted in 1996 voluntarily.
The agency said it agreed to the licences in order to enable Yorkshire to meet its water supply deficits.
Yorkshire came under severe criticism and was penalised by the industry regulator Ofwat for its handling of a severe drought in 1995 when it verged on rota cuts in essential domestic supplies.
Since then, new management has been put in place and the company said earlier this year that it would not seek supply restrictions or drought orders this summer.

"We welcome the progress made by Yorkshire Water and the water-saving efforts of its customers. This gives us a clear signal that at least some of the time-limited licences have now served their particular purpose," the agency's north east regional water manager David Rooke said in a statement.
The rivers affected are the Ure, Wharfe and Ouse.
